name: Forensic accounting
method: Reconcile every unit of a total to an independent total; test digit distributions for fabrication.
instruments: A reconciliation join between two sources; a Benford first-digit test.
receipt: A reconciliation table with the unexplained residual, and the Benford test statistic.

name: Epidemiology
verbs: link a cause to an outcome
method: Compare exposed and unexposed groups over the same period (difference-in-differences, case-control); look for dose-response.
instruments: A 2×2 table or difference-in-differences estimate with an unexposed control group.
receipt: The effect with its confidence interval, and the control group that rules out a common shock.

name: Investigative journalism
method: Two independent sources per key fact; a dated document trail.
instruments: A source log: claim, source 1, source 2, date.
receipt: Each key claim with two independent sources, or marked single-source.

name: Site reliability engineering
method: A blameless timeline from raw logs; service level objectives with error budgets.
instruments: A log query that builds a minute-by-minute timeline; a service level indicator query.
receipt: The timeline with the trigger and the contributing factors, and the error budget burned.

name: Clinical trials and biostatistics
verbs: prove a change causes an effect
method: Pre-register the prediction, randomize, size the sample by power analysis, and analyse as planned.
instruments: A prediction file written before the data is read; a power calculation; a randomized holdout.
receipt: The prediction file (written before the data was read), n from the power calculation, and the effect with its interval.

name: Short-seller research
method: Channel checks: compare each reported number with an observable proxy from outside the company.
instruments: An independent data source set against the reported metric.
receipt: The claim, the independent measure, and the gap.

name: Editing (books, film)
method: Reverse-outline the draft, then cut every section that doesn't advance the one point.
instruments: A reverse outline: one line per section stating its point.
receipt: Word count before and after, and the reverse outline with the cut sections marked.

name: Aviation safety and human factors
method: Failure modes and effects analysis; checklists for critical steps; read-back.
instruments: An FMEA table scored severity × occurrence × detection.
receipt: FMEA rows with risk priority numbers, and the mitigation for the top row.

name: Operations research and queueing
method: Model the system (Little's law, M/M/c queues, linear programming) and simulate before changing it.
instruments: A queueing model or LP solver checked against observed throughput.
receipt: Modelled vs observed wait and throughput, and the objective value of the chosen allocation.

name: Security red team
verbs: find how it breaks under an adversary
method: Threat model (STRIDE), an attack tree, then real exploit attempts.
instruments: An attack tree and a proof-of-concept script run against the real system.
receipt: Each leaf of the attack tree tried, with the working proof of concept or the blocked result.

name: Performance engineering
method: Measure first: profile under a realistic load, fix the top frame, and measure again.
instruments: A profiler (flame graph) and a benchmark with a fixed workload and repeat runs.
receipt: The before and after benchmark with variance, and the flame-graph frame that moved.

name: UX research
method: Watch five real users try the task without help, and count where they fail.
instruments: A task-based usability test script and a session recording or transcript.
receipt: Task success rate per step, and the quoted stall points.

name: Actuarial science
method: Fit a loss distribution to historical claims and price from its tail, not its mean.
instruments: A fitted frequency-severity model on historical loss data.
receipt: The fitted distribution, the 99th-percentile loss, and the reserve it implies.

name: Supply chain and logistics
method: Map the flow end to end with lead times and inventory at each node; size buffers from demand variability.
instruments: A value-stream map with lead time and inventory per step; a safety-stock calculation.
receipt: Lead time per step, the share that is waiting, and the buffer sized from variance.

name: Game design
verbs: make people want to come back
method: Design the core loop and its reward schedule, then playtest and tune numbers from telemetry.
instruments: A core-loop diagram and playtest telemetry (drop-off per step).
receipt: The loop, the drop-off per step from a playtest, and the number tuned.

name: Intelligence analysis
method: Analysis of competing hypotheses: score every piece of evidence against every hypothesis and keep the least-contradicted one.
instruments: An ACH matrix of evidence × hypotheses.
receipt: The matrix, the surviving hypothesis, and the single piece of evidence that would flip it.

name: Litigation and contract law
method: Read the text literally, find the strongest opposing reading, and test every clause against an adversarial counterparty.
instruments: A clause-by-clause adversarial read with precedent or source cited.
receipt: Each clause with its hostile reading, and the rewrite that closes it.

name: Ethnography
method: Observe people doing the real work in place, and record what they do, not what they say.
instruments: Field notes or a screen recording of the real workflow.
receipt: The workarounds observed, each quoted or timestamped, and the rule each reveals.
